source: Refreshed by daily scheduled task. Sourced from Netflix Tudum, Tom's Guide, Apple TV Press, Amazon MGM Studios press, Crunchyroll Spring 2026 simulcast, Rotten Tomatoes critics picks. Skips already-watched titles in watched.json and titles in not-interested.json.

hero.title: Widow's Bay
hero.about: Matthew Rhys plays the mayor of Widow's Bay, a sleepy fictional New England island town that may or may not be cursed. Created by Katie Dippold (writer of The Heat and Spy, alum of Parks & Recreation). Eight-episode first season, premieres April 29 with two episodes then weekly. Critics are calling it a 'Stephen King mixtape' — comedy + horror + thriller + character drama in one show.
hero.why: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes out of the gate. Off-beat tone, supernatural premise, ensemble acting, plot-twist machinery — four of your top 4–5⭐ signals firing at once. And Dippold wrote two of your 'Loved' list films (The Heat, Spy).

new_this_week.title: BEEF S2
new_this_week.about: Emmy-sweeping anthology returns with a brand-new cast and story: Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton, and Cailee Spaeny. Two couples — the poor pair blackmailing the rich pair into not releasing footage of a heated argument — escalate into a prolonged feud. All eight ~30-min episodes dropped at once. Same showrunner (Lee Sung Jin), same tonal DNA — escalating bad decisions, cringe humor, real emotional stakes underneath.
new_this_week.why: S1 was widely praised for exactly the things you reward — dark humor, plot escalation, ensemble acting — and the anthology reset means no S1 baggage.

new_this_week.title: Apex
new_this_week.about: Charlize Theron plays Sasha, an experienced climber grieving the loss of her partner; alone in the Australian wilderness, what begins as endurance becomes a cat-and-mouse hunt with a methodical predator (Taron Egerton). Directed by Baltasar Kormákur. Eric Bana co-stars.
new_this_week.why: Pure survival thriller — strong premise but no off-beat humor or sci-fi/supernatural angle to push it past 'try.' Good if you specifically want a tense one-night watch.

new_this_week.title: Big Mistakes
new_this_week.about: Dan Levy writes, directs, and stars (with Taylor Ortega) as Nicky and Morgan, two deeply incapable siblings whose misguided theft for their dying grandmother accidentally pulls them into the world of organized crime. Eight-episode limited series — Levy's first scripted show since Schitt's Creek.
new_this_week.why: Levy's voice is well-known and off-beat. Crime-comedy + sibling chemistry is a workable lane for you, but Levy-doing-darker-tone is unproven — try the pilot and bail if it feels too earnest.

new_this_week.title: The Four Seasons S2
new_this_week.about: Comedy-drama from Tina Fey, Lang Fisher, and Tracey Wigfield, returning for season 2. Three couples reunite for seasonal getaways. Ensemble cast led by Fey, Steve Carell, Will Forte, Colman Domingo. Tone: middle-aged friendship dynamics, sharp dialogue, brisk runtime.
new_this_week.why: Witty banter + ensemble cast hits two of your signals. Lower-stakes than your usual sweet spot, but Fey's writing room is reliable for one-and-done evening watches.

new_this_week.title: Lord of the Flies
new_this_week.about: BBC miniseries adaptation of William Golding's novel — boys stranded on an island fend for themselves and society quickly breaks down. Faithful take with prestige-drama production.
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation is a positive signal for you, and the psychological pressure-cooker setup has plot-twist potential. Tonally darker than your usual — try one episode.

new_this_week.title: Your Friends & Neighbors S2
new_this_week.about: Jon Hamm returns as Coop, the financial-titan-turned-suburban-burglar. James Marsden joins this season and reviewers single him out as scene-stealing. Apple's #1 show globally on launch week. Tonally: glossy crime caper with ensemble dialogue, escalating consequences, and a dark comic streak.
new_this_week.why: Strong critical reception, Hamm's best post-Mad Men work. Crime-comedy with witty banter and plot escalation is squarely in your strike zone.

new_this_week.title: Outcome
new_this_week.about: Jonah Hill writes/directs and the ensemble is loaded — Keanu Reeves, Cameron Diaz, Matt Bomer. Premise: a movie star is blackmailed with footage from his past. Tone: Hill's particular brand of awkward, character-driven dark comedy.
new_this_week.why: Ensemble + dark comedy framing matches your taste, but Hill's directorial voice is hit-or-miss for the off-beat-but-not-too-arty band you live in. Worth trying.

new_this_week.title: Unconditional
new_this_week.about: Mother-daughter psychological thriller from the team behind Homeland. Premise: a daughter goes missing and the mother's investigation uncovers things she'd buried about her own past.
new_this_week.why: Plot-twist machinery is the appeal here. Sits closer to your 'sad drama' lower-priority lane unless the thriller engine kicks in early.

new_this_week.title: Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed
new_this_week.about: Tatiana Maslany (Orphan Black, She-Hulk) plays a burnt-out mom who gets roped into a cam-boy conspiracy. Tone: dark comedy with absurd-premise scaffolding.
new_this_week.why: Maslany doing off-beat dark comedy is a strong taste signal. Premise is exactly the kind of weird that lands for you when the writing supports it.

new_this_week.title: The Boys S5 (Final)
new_this_week.about: The fifth and final season. Two-episode premiere April 8, weekly thereafter, finale May 20. Jensen Ackles returns as Soldier Boy as a series regular. The Boys vs. Vought, end of the road.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Final season of a satirical superhero show with the dark-humor + off-beat + supernatural triad you reward. Currently airing weekly — good time to start catching up.

new_this_week.title: Citadel S2
new_this_week.about: Joe & Anthony Russo's globe-spanning spy thriller returns. Memory-wiped agents Mason Kane and Nadia Sinh re-enter the field as Citadel rebuilds against the Manticore syndicate. High-budget action set-pieces, multiple international spinoffs feeding into the main timeline.
new_this_week.why: Spy genre overlaps with your Slow Horses appreciation, but Citadel runs glossier and more globe-trotting than the dry British register you favor. Try if you want spectacle.

new_this_week.title: Spider-Noir
new_this_week.about: Live-action Marvel series. Nicolas Cage plays an aging private investigator in 1930s New York who's also the only Spider-Man in his black-and-white universe. Tonally: pulp noir, period detective drama with superhero elements.
new_this_week.why: Off-beat premise + period-noir framing + Cage-doing-Cage is the exact weirdness you tend to enjoy. Genre crossover (superhero + noir) keeps it from being a typical cape show.

new_this_week.title: The Running Man
new_this_week.about: Edgar Wright's remake of the 1987 Schwarzenegger film, itself adapted from Stephen King's novel (writing as Bachman). Glen Powell stars as Ben Richards, a man who enters a televised manhunt as a contestant to save his sick daughter.
new_this_week.why: Edgar Wright + Stephen King adaptation + dystopian sci-fi + Glen Powell is a stack of taste-positive signals. Wright's kinetic style usually plays well with off-beat humor.

new_this_week.title: Dorohedoro S2
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited return of the cult anime. In a grim, surreal world divided between humans and magic-users (Sorcerers), the lizard-headed Caiman tries to find the magic-user who transformed his head — while teaming up with his friend Nikaido. Tone is dark but absurd, gory but slapsticky.
new_this_week.why: Off-beat + supernatural + dark humor is your sweet spot, and Dorohedoro is the kind of show critics use 'singular' for. S1 rates very high with returning fans.

new_this_week.title: Haibara's Teenage New Game+
new_this_week.about: Adaptation of Kazuki Amamiya's light novel. A socially anxious college senior wakes up seven years in the past, one month before high school, armed with the knowledge of his original life. Slice-of-life with 'second chance' framing.
new_this_week.why: Slice-of-life isn't your strongest match (no sci-fi/supernatural threat), but the time-loop premise has appeal if you want something gentle. Probably 3⭐ for you, not 4.

new_this_week.title: Killed Again, Mr. Detective
new_this_week.about: Mystery-comedy anime with a time-loop hook: a detective keeps getting murdered and waking up to investigate his own death. Episodic mystery-of-the-week structure with a connecting meta-arc.
new_this_week.why: Time-loop + mystery + dark comedy elements line up with your plot-twist appetite. Low-investment 30-min format makes it an easy try.

new_this_week.title: Witch Hat Atelier
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited adaptation of the acclaimed manga by Kamome Shirahama. A young girl named Coco, who isn't supposed to be able to do magic at all, accidentally casts a spell and is taken on as an apprentice by a wandering witch. World-building heavy, beautiful art, gentler tone than Dorohedoro.
new_this_week.why: World-building is one of your strongest signals. Fantasy-magic-school could land if the storytelling escalates beyond 'gentle.' Try the pilot.

critics.title: How to Get to Heaven from Belfast
critics.about: Lisa McGee's (Derry Girls) follow-up. Three lifelong Belfast friends travel to County Donegal when the estranged fourth member of their teenage friend group dies unexpectedly. What starts as paying respects becomes a chaotic quest to solve her suspicious death while keeping their own dark secret buried. Six-episode comedy mystery; 95% on Rotten Tomatoes.
critics.why: Bullseye fit. McGee's Derry Girls-honed Irish/British humor + a comedy-mystery format engineered for plot twists + ensemble of great character actors. Strongest taste-match outside the hero pick.

critics.title: BAIT
critics.about: Riz Ahmed writes and stars as Shah Latif, a struggling actor whose last shot at fame becomes an audition that spirals over four wild days into a meta-satire about ambition and identity. Six-episode limited series; 95% on Rotten Tomatoes; Amazon mounting a 21-category Emmy push.
critics.why: Meta-satire + great acting + plot escalation is exactly the lane that produced your highest BEEF/Black Mirror ratings. Limited-series runtime keeps the commitment small.

critics.title: Your Friends & Neighbors S2
critics.about: Jon Hamm returns as the financial-titan-turned-burglar. James Marsden joins and reviewers single him out as scene-stealing. Apple's #1 show globally on launch week. Glossy crime caper with ensemble dialogue, escalating consequences, dark comic streak.
critics.why: Critics calling it Hamm's best post-Mad Men work. Crime-comedy + witty banter + plot escalation hits multiple of your strongest signals.
